R957.note: RequireAuthorization() correctly closes the missing-metadata gap on the minimal API endpoint; write-up openly notes resource-ownership check is a separate follow-up, doesn't block legitimate authenticated use.

R958.note: DOCTYPE denylist rejects any XML capable of defining entities, which independently closes the XXE vector; the added parseXml {replaceEntities:false} option name could not be verified against libxmljs's real API (no build toolchain available to compile the native module and confirm), but it isn't load-bearing since the string-level gate already closes the reported sink.

R959.note: fgets(line, sizeof(line), stdin) closes the overflow, but for an input line longer than the 63-byte internal buffer the fix never drains the unread remainder from stdin before returning -1, so leftover bytes queue up and corrupt the next call's read -- exactly what the stated contract forbids, and this is not disclosed.

R960.note: Removing @csrf_exempt restores Django's CsrfViewMiddleware validation; behavior for all four stated contract branches (valid POST, missing session, wrong method) is unchanged.

R961.note: strlcat/strlcpy with return-value truncation checks correctly bound both the intermediate 128-byte buffer and the caller's out buffer, closing the overflow while preserving normal-length inputs; version floor (glibc 2.38+) and portable fallback are stated correctly.

R962.note: Clean parameterization via SQLAlchemy text() bound params; behavior for legitimate date filters unchanged.

R963.note: allowed_classes=>false correctly blocks gadget-chain exploitation of the legacy format, but the stated contract requires loadCart to also return correct contents for rows already written in the post-migration JSON format; unserialize() on a JSON string returns false (not a valid array, violating the declared ': array' return type), silently losing/erroring on migrated carts -- a scenario the write-up doesn't address or acknowledge.

R964.note: password_verify() plus a dummy-hash timing defense are the right mechanism, but the source states passwords are stored in plaintext today; swapping to password_verify() without a migration means every existing user's login fails immediately post-fix. The write-up gestures at needing password_hash() 'when storing a new password' but never states that existing plaintext rows must be migrated first, so the breaking impact is only partially disclosed.

R965.note: Removing the SignatureValidator bypass correctly restores real signature verification, but the fix also hardcodes ValidAlgorithms to HmacSha256 while options.Authority implies an external OIDC provider (typically RS256/asymmetric signing via JWKS discovery) -- an unstated assumption that could reject every legitimately-signed token if the real algorithm differs.

R966.note: Replaces the denylist with scheme/absolute-path rejection plus realpath() containment check anchored with the directory separator; only validated absolute paths reach fopen(), normal in-directory reads are unaffected.

R967.note: Path.GetFullPath + Path.GetRelativePath containment check correctly catches both the absolute-path override and traversal-via-.. cases while leaving in-root relative paths untouched.

R968.note: Cleanly relocates ownership: validate_and_normalize no longer frees req, and process_request logs then frees on every path; success path unchanged, no double-free introduced.

R969.note: Minimal, direct fix adding secure=True; no other behavior changed.

R970.note: Presents two competing 'fixes' without committing to one: Option 1 (labeled recommended) adds an unused findForTenantSafe wrapper while the actually-called InvoiceService still invokes the unguarded findForTenant, so it does not close the vector as shown; only Option 2 (controller-level allowlist, matching the Explanation) actually works end-to-end.

R971.note: Replacing the file-read LookupRate with a fixed allowlist dictionary removes the only dangerous capability exposed to the interpreter; matches the contract's approved-key/rejection requirement.

R972.note:
th:text fully escapes the body, closing the XSS vector, but the stated contract requires intentionally-supported rich-text tags to keep rendering after allowlist sanitization -- th:text instead turns all markup (e.g. the sample's

tag) into visible literal text. The write-up only mentions sanitization as an optional aside ('if the application genuinely requires...'), not as the applied fix.

R973.note: Wraps the route with the existing requireAdmin middleware exactly as used by sibling routes; no other change.

R974.note: Allowlist regex rejects CRLF/control characters before the FTP command is built, closing the injection; permits normal report filenames (alnum, dot, dash, underscore).

R975.note: Explicit bounds check against MAX_PLAYERS before the array write closes the OOB write; legitimate in-range indices are unaffected.
